title: Help
description: A guide to working with the system. The sections you see match your permissions — another role sees different ones.

topics.title: Signing in and the work screen

blocks.p: Sign in with a phone number or email and a password. With Telegram linked, a one-time code works instead of a password. Each role lands on its own screen: reception on the front desk, the doctor in the consulting room, the cashier at the register.

steps: Top-left holds the branch switcher — the queue, the register and most lists show the selected branch only
Cmd+K (or Ctrl+K) anywhere — quick patient search
The bell shows system notifications; the avatar menu holds language and Security (two-step sign-in)

blocks.warn: If a screen looks empty, check the branch first: what you just created may live in another one. The branch choice is remembered per computer — on a shared machine, glance at it before working.

faq.q: Every screen is always empty — what now?
faq.a: Your account may not be attached to any branch. An administrator sets your branch in Settings → Staff.

blocks.p: The left menu is built from your permissions: a cashier sees the Register, a lab tech sees the Laboratory. A missing item is access control, not a malfunction.

blocks.tip: The owner or an administrator can grant (or revoke) an individual permission per person: Settings → Staff → row menu → Permissions. It takes effect immediately and the menu updates on the spot.

steps: Patients → New patient (or the quick add on the front desk)
Name and phone matter most; fill the date of birth and sex too — laboratory reference values depend on them
The Outpatient/Inpatient choice sets the patient type
Save

blocks.warn: Duplicates are detected only by the EXACT same phone or the EXACT same name plus birth date. "Create anyway" is one click — search the list first. Cleaning up afterwards is management-only.

faq.q: A typo in the name — will fixing it break old receipts?
faq.a: No, fix it freely. Search, old invoices and lab results all show the corrected name immediately.

blocks.p: They are different things. Delete hides the card — history, debt and deposit vanish with it (management still sees it marked deleted, but there is NO undo). Merge moves everything — visits, invoices, lab orders, deposits — onto the primary card.

blocks.warn: Found a duplicate — do NOT delete it; ask an administrator to Merge. Merge is irreversible too: the deposits add up and everything moves to one card. Check which card is the primary before pressing.

blocks.p: The patient card's Documents tab takes PDFs and photos (up to 20 MB; photos are recompressed). The Overview tab records signed consents (personal data, procedures).

blocks.warn: Deleting a document destroys the file forever — it is not in "deleted" either. Download a copy first. (Deleting a patient card, by contrast, hides rather than destroys.)

steps: A walk-in arrives: add them on the Reception screen — they join the queue at once
A booked patient arrives: check them in from the list and send them to the queue
The doctor works with "Call next"; finishing opens the visit record
The queue resets every midnight and is per branch

blocks.tip: Past times cannot be booked — a patient already seen at 9:00 simply goes in as a walk-in.

blocks.warn: Transferring a ticket to another doctor CHANGES its number (A-005 → B-012) — tell the patient the new number, or they will wait for one that never comes up on the screen.

blocks.p: Free slots come from the doctor's working schedule. "No free slots" almost always means the doctor's hours are not set up for this branch (Staff → Schedule).

blocks.warn: Rescheduling checks only for double-booking, NOT the doctor's schedule — you can move a visit outside working hours. Watch the date and time yourself.

Cancel and No-show are one-way: a wrong click means booking again. "No-show" also counts against the patient. A recurring course silently skips occupied dates — check the "created X / skipped Y" summary.

steps: "Call next" from the queue — the patient comes in
At the end press "Finish" on the ticket — the visit record opens
Fill complaints, examination, diagnosis (ICD-10), prescriptions, referrals
When everything is in — "Complete visit"

blocks.warn: Press "Complete visit" only when EVERYTHING is entered: a completed visit accepts no more diagnoses or prescriptions. A mistake noticed later goes in only as a formal amendment.

blocks.tip: Templates fill EMPTY fields only and never overwrite typed text. If a template "did nothing", the field was already taken.

faq.q: I need a sick colleague's patient — they are not in my list?
faq.a: By default a doctor sees only their own visits. If the owner enables the "branch-wide" mode in Settings → Clinic, doctors of one branch see each other's visits.

blocks.p: A test ticked inside the visit reaches the laboratory worklist IMMEDIATELY — it does not wait for payment. Send the patient to the register first, or the tech may process an unpaid order.
ONE register per branch. Opening takes two opening floats: cash and transfers (card/online). Closing counts both. Whoever holds the shift permission may close — not only the opener.

steps: Register → Open shift → enter the cash and transfer opening floats
During the day: cash needs an open shift; card/online go through without one but land in nobody's drawer
At closing, compare the box against the "expected in register" figure (it already includes the opening float)
If the transfer book holds anything — count it, or write why it could not be counted

blocks.warn: Once a shift closes, its payments and expenses FREEZE: no void, no edits. Review the day before counting out.

blocks.tip: A payment taken from a patient's deposit never shows in the day's takings — correct: that money was counted on the day it was deposited.

topics.title: Void and Refund are different verbs

blocks.p: VOID — "this money was never taken": erase a mistyped amount the same day; the invoice becomes payable again. REFUND — real money went back to the patient: it leaves the register as an outflow.

blocks.warn: Void works only while the shift is open. A refund comes out of the register open NOW: refunding yesterday's sale today closes today's drawer short by that amount — not an error.

blocks.tip: "Refund to balance" now genuinely credits the patient's account for future payments. A partly refunded invoice stays "Paid" — see the Refunds table inside the invoice for what actually went back.

blocks.p: A cash expense needs the open shift and lowers the expected cash. A card expense touches no register. The payment method cannot be changed later — pick it right the first time.

topics.title: Why can't the cashier see the invoice?

blocks.p: The "New invoice" window creates a DRAFT. A draft is invisible to the register and absent from the patient's debt — it becomes payable only after "Issue". The front desk's quick sale does this by itself.

blocks.tip: The reception's pending strip shows the latest 50 unpaid invoices, current branch only. The complete picture of debts is in Debtors, clinic-wide.

blocks.p: "Pay now" in the quick sale takes the full amount; anything less stays "On account". You cannot record more than what is due: change from a large note comes from the drawer, only the real amount is recorded.

steps: On the Inpatient page — "Admit" → find the patient
Department, ward, bed, diagnosis — the case history (KT number) opens
The Case history tab keeps complaints, anamnesis, the daily diary
"Print" produces form 003

blocks.p: A patient can be in only one active stay. Discharge opens only once this stay's unpaid services are settled.

topics.title: The treatment sheet — every mark moves money

blocks.p: The doctor orders ("5 days, twice a day"), the sheet gets a cell per dose. "Given" charges the service to the patient at once; "Refused" cancels the charge. The price is the one in force on the DAY of the mark.

blocks.warn: A cell never returns to blank — only given↔refused. A mark already on an invoice cannot change at all. "Stop" fires on a single unconfirmed click and cannot be undone — the course must be ordered again.

blocks.tip: Marking is its own permission (the nurse and the front desk have it; the doctor's default set does not). A doctor who cannot press the cells — that is by design.

blocks.p: The patient card's Payments tab lists unpaid services. Tick what the patient pays now — the invoice reaches the register instantly, the rest stays owed.

topics.title: The lab flow at a glance

blocks.p: Only services in a Laboratory-kind category reach the lab. The moment such a service is sold, the order appears on the tech's worklist; after results are entered and approved, the patient is notified and the PDF opens in three places: the patient card, the patient cabinet, and the Telegram bot.

blocks.warn: An approved result is FROZEN — a mistake means a new order. A refund does NOT remove the order from the lab worklist — tell the lab separately.

blocks.tip: A detailed guide exists as its own page — ask the owner for the "Laboratory handbook" link.

blocks.p: A price takes effect from its date; history is kept. Invoice amounts freeze at creation — later price changes never touch old invoices.

blocks.warn: Give a branch its own price and it DETACHES from the clinic-wide one: raising the default later does nothing there. After any default change, review branch prices and PACKAGES by hand — package prices do not follow.
Discount rules are reference-only for now: the register does NOT apply them; discounts are typed manually at sale.

blocks.tip: Deleting a service actually deactivates it: old invoices are untouched, and the "Inactive" filter finds it for reactivation via edit.

blocks.p: In the Revenue report, "by day" and "by method" are money actually COLLECTED (by payment date). "By category" and "by doctor" are amounts BILLED (invoice lines), debt included. They legitimately differ.

blocks.tip: Dashboard revenue is for the ONE selected branch. The register's "expected" figure is another number again: it contains the opening float.

faq.q: A patient shows both a deposit and a debt — how?
faq.a: The system never nets them: the deposit sits apart from the debt. Settling debt from a deposit is a deliberate act at the register.

steps: Settings → Staff → Add staff member
Pick a role — the menu is built from it
If needed: row menu → Permissions — grant or revoke individual rights

blocks.tip: The plan limit counts ACTIVE staff only. Hiring a replacement? Suspend (archive) the old account first — the seat frees up.

blocks.warn: The "Administrator" role opens Settings but cannot SAVE much of it (clinic requisites, branches — owner rights). The TV display token is owner-only too.

blocks.p: In receipt settings the logo saves the moment it is picked; other options need the Save button below. Messages to patients go out in the CLINIC's default language — even if the template exists in all four.

blocks.warn: The Birthday and Debt-reminder templates do not send themselves yet — those sections are groundwork for a future version.

topics.title: What happens when the subscription ends?

blocks.p: The clinic is not switched off — it goes read-only: signing in, opening cards and reports keep working, but new records will not save. Everything returns after payment.

sections.title: Patient apps: Telegram and the cabinet

blocks.p: The patient presses /start and shares their number — matching the card's main OR alternative phone links them. From then on: appointment reminders (24h and 2h ahead), live queue position, ready lab results (with PDFs), documents.

blocks.tip: Patients can cancel an appointment from the bot, but the button closes 2 hours before the start — after that, only a phone call to the clinic.

blocks.p: The cabinet signs in by phone number and SMS code. Note: it recognises only the card's MAIN number — the alternative one works in Telegram only. Lab results are always open in the cabinet; visit history (diagnoses, prescriptions) appears after the clinic's approval — requests land in Patients → Record access.

blocks.warn: A patient says "no code arrived": the code goes to Telegram first; without Telegram an SMS is sent — and if the SMS provider is not yet connected (log mode), the code never reaches them at all. Advise such patients to link Telegram.
